title: Enterprise model request escalation and catalog triage playbook
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Create a repeatable triage and escalation playbook for enterprise-origin model catalog requests (new model additions, version pin requests, planned deprecations, and eval/gating waivers). The goal is to reduce lead time for enterprise requests, surface risk signals early, and standardize artifacts required for approval so PM/Eng/Trust can make timely decisions. This playbook covers intake form requirements, automated signal checks, priority scoring, SLA tiers, stakeholder ownership, and communication templates.
background: Customers and sales have escalated requests that vary widely in scope and risk — from a one-off model pin for regulatory reasons to requests to onboard a brand-new foundation model. Current handling is ad hoc; we lack consistent artifact gating (eval suites, latency budgets, KMS confirmation) which increases time-to-approve and operational surprises during rollout.
objectives: Cut average time-to-decision for enterprise model requests from current ~18 business days to <= 7 business days for P1 requests
Ensure every approved model has a minimum set of artifacts (eval report, privacy/RAD checklist, performance profile, rollback plan)
Define clear SLA tiers and escalation paths for requests with compliance or data residency requirements
Provide automation hooks (pre-check scripts) to surface obvious blockers before human review
triage_runbook: 1) Intake: Customer/AE fills enterprise-model-request form (linked) with required artifacts attached.
2) Automated pre-checks: run eval-harness smoke tests (perf baseline, hallucination quick checks), config compatibility, license scan, and KMS/region availability. Pre-checks return pass/warn/fail.
3) Priority scoring: apply weighted heuristic (security flag, SLA need, revenue at risk, model novelty, infra compatibility) to assign P0/P1/P2.
4) Ownership assignment: PMT lead assigns to Catalog PM (owner) and Eng lead reviewers based on request type.
5) Gate checklist: require minimum artifacts depending on type (see artifact matrix). If items missing, return to requester with templates.
6) Rapid committee: For P0/P1, convene Catalog Review Committee (PM, Eng, Trust, Sales rep) and schedule decision within SLA window.
7) Approval steps: signed agreement on pinning/deprecation window, rollout plan, fallbacks, canary metrics, and monitoring dashboards.
8) Post-decision: update catalog metadata, trigger rollout (canary -> staged -> global) and add to scheduled deprecation/pin list if applicable.
9) Review: after 30 days of run, capture lessons, cost signal, and any quality regressions; feed into Optimize recommendations.
artifact_matrix: New model add: eval report (accuracy/robustness across enterprise prompts), latency & cost profile, license + provenance doc, security/privacy assessment, suggested quantization profile, KMS/region compatibility note
Version pin request: justification memo (regression or regulatory), comparative eval vs default runtime model, estimated additional cost, rollback criterion, requested pin duration
Deprecation request: usage metrics, migration guide for customers, sunset timeline, compensate/notification plan
Eval gate waiver: explicit risk acceptance form, compensating controls, proposed monitoring signals
sla_matrix: P0: 48 hours decision window. Applies to outages, high-severity customer-blocking requests. Committee meets immediately.
P1: 7 business days. Enterprise feature requests or regulatory pins. Standard committee cadence.
P2: 30 business days. Low-risk additions or non-urgent deprecations.
P3: Backlog. No SLA; batched into quarterly catalog review.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with templates and intake form link
Automated pre-checks implemented as a GitHub Action that annotates the Linear ticket with pre-check results
Committee membership and meeting cadence defined, calendar invites configured
Metrics dashboard for time-to-decision and post-approval regressions created in Looker
Sample run-through completed with two live enterprise requests and retrospective notes captured
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-burdening requesters with heavy artifact requirements -> Mitigation: tiered artifact matrix and fast-track for low-risk cases
Risk: Committee bottleneck causes SLA misses -> Mitigation: define delegation policy and pre-approved playbook for repeatable request patterns
Risk: Automation false-negative/positive -> Mitigation: surface raw logs and allow manual override with justification
success_metrics: Median time-to-decision for P1 requests <= 7 business days
>= 90% of approved models have full artifact set attached
Reduction in catalog-related incidents during first 60 days after onboarding by 30%
implementation_plan: Week 1-2: Finalize intake form and template artifacts; draft Confluence playbook
Week 3: Implement pre-check GitHub Action and wire to ticket annotations
Week 4: Define committee membership and onboard reviewers; create Looker dashboard
Week 5-6: Pilot with two enterprise customers (one pin request, one new model add), collect feedback
Week 7: Iterate on playbook and roll into broader catalog process
notes: Early conversations with Sales and Trust indicate most friction points are around KMS confirmation and eval artifacts. We should add a KMS check to the pre-checks and provide a short KMS confirmation template for customers.
